items.title: Closed restore-point object contract
items.statement: A restore-point artifact is a JSON object governed by a fixed schema identifier and title; undeclared top-level properties are rejected.

items.title: Required identity, lineage, status, retention, routing, and payload fields
items.statement: The object must provide schema and artifact identity, project/run/attempt lineage, creation time, projection freshness and health, retention class, routing references, and a type-specific payload.

items.title: Artifact classification is invariant
items.statement: schema_id and artifact_type are fixed to the v1 restore-point schema and restore_point classification respectively.

items.title: Routing and payload minimum cardinality
items.statement: At least one non-empty routing reference and at least one payload property are required.

items.title: Creation time is not format validated
items.statement: created_at_utc is only a non-empty string; the contract does not require a date-time format, UTC offset, canonical precision, or parseability.
items.impact: Malformed or incomparable timestamps can pass structural validation and undermine ordering, retention, and recovery operations.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose timestamp syntax, precision, parsing, and normalization behavior.

items.title: Projection and retention state vocabularies are unconstrained
items.statement: projection_freshness, projection_health, and retention_class accept arbitrary strings; allowed states, meanings, transitions, and recovery consequences are not specified.
items.impact: Producers and consumers can emit or interpret incompatible state values, preventing deterministic lifecycle and recovery behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent state vocabularies, transition rules, invalid-state handling, and retention semantics.

items.title: Type payload has no restore-point semantics
items.statement: type_payload need only be a non-empty object; its required contents, restore behavior, integrity checks, size bounds, confidentiality, and compatibility rules are unspecified.
items.impact: Structurally valid artifacts can lack the data needed to restore state, while producers and consumers can disagree on payload shape and limits.
items.builder_discretion: Builders control payload schema, nesting, validation, limits, protection, and version evolution.

items.title: Reference integrity and propagation behavior are unspecified
items.statement: Thread, node, provider-attempt, usage-event, receipt, producer, actor, detail, content, source-surface, and routing references have string-level shape only; namespace, existence, authorization, cardinality limits, deduplication, and resolution failure behavior are absent.
items.impact: Dangling, ambiguous, unauthorized, duplicate, or excessively large reference sets can validate, leaving consumers unable to resolve or safely propagate the artifact.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose reference namespaces, integrity and access checks, resolution failure handling, ordering, deduplication, and propagation semantics.

items.title: Authority, ownership, consumer, security, and recovery rules are absent
items.statement: The contract provides optional producer_ref and actor_ref strings but does not define who may create, mutate, retain, read, route, consume, or restore an artifact, nor how failures or privacy-sensitive contents are handled.
items.impact: Implementations can diverge on ownership and authorization, expose sensitive restore data, or fail non-deterministically during restoration and cleanup.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must define authority, ownership, consumers, access control, privacy handling, failure states, retries, rollback, retention execution, and recovery ownership.

items.title: Acceptance oracle is structural only
items.statement: JSON Schema validation can reject unknown top-level properties, missing required fields, wrong primitive types, incorrect constants, empty required identifiers, empty routing arrays, and empty payload objects; it cannot establish referential, semantic, restoration, security, or lifecycle correctness.
items.impact: A schema-valid object is not necessarily a usable or safe restore point.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must add all semantic and executable restoration oracles beyond schema validation.

items.title: No GUI surface is defined by this schema
items.statement: The authoritative line defines a machine-readable runtime artifact object and contains no user-interface field, presentation rule, or user interaction contract; GUI truth is not applicable to this isolated schema contract.

dimension_assessments.summary: Structural validation behavior is defined, but restoration behavior is not.
The schema can classify and structurally validate restore-point artifacts, but it does not specify an executable restore capability.
The accepted top-level object shape, required inputs, optional references, routing array, and payload object are defined.
A closed JSON Schema contract with fixed classification and minimum field/cardinality constraints is present.
Projection and retention fields exist, but state vocabularies and transitions are undefined.
Producer and actor references do not establish permissions or decision authority.
No owner is designated for creation, retention, restoration, mutation, or cleanup.
No consumers or their interpretation and resolution obligations are identified.
This isolated artifact-schema line defines no GUI surface or presentation contract.
Resolution failures, invalid state, restore failure, retry, rollback, and recovery ownership are unspecified.
No access, confidentiality, integrity, privacy, or sensitive-payload handling rules are imposed.
Routing references exist, but resolution, deduplication, ordering, authorization, and propagation semantics are absent.
Timestamp, retention execution, cleanup, observability, and restore-operation rules are incomplete.
Payload, receipt-reference, and routing-reference sizes have no upper bounds or performance expectations.
The schema has a fixed v1 identifier, but payload versioning, compatibility, and migration rules are absent.
Structural JSON Schema validation exists, but no semantic or executable restoration oracle is defined.
Builders retain consequential discretion over timestamp syntax, state vocabularies, payload shape, reference integrity, authority, security, lifecycle, and recovery.
Core restore-point meaning remains ambiguous because payload semantics, reference namespaces, state meanings, and operational rules are not defined.
